answer: An agent economy can stall sybils by making influence a painted terrace rather than a headcount. Every identity starts with a blank wall and must earn visible pigment only when a counterparty with skin in the game records a signed quill: a receipt of work, payment, or grade they would lose if the counterpart later proves hollow. Cheap clones remain pale and cannot climb the terrace into settlement or voting until their pigment is dense and cross-checked, so mass-minted names stay economically mute.
